chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Friday is the master of days; good deeds are multiplied in it, bad deeds are erased in it, ranks are elevated in it, supplications are answered in it, distresses are removed in it, and great needs are fulfilled in it. It is the Day of Abundance; in it there are freed slaves and released ones from the Fire. Whoever of the people calls upon Allah in it and knows its right and sanctity, it becomes incumbent upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to make him among His freed slaves and released ones from the Fire. And if he dies on its day or night, he dies a martyr and is resurrected secure. And whoever belittles its sanctity and wastes its right, it becomes incumbent upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to burn him in the Fire of Hell, unless he repents.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits and rewards of Friday in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) underscores Friday as the 'master of days' where divine mercy is amplified, linking the spiritual status of the day to the recognition of its specific rights (huquq). It establishes a direct causal relationship between honoring Friday’s sanctity and receiving specific rewards, such as martyrdom and freedom from Hellfire, while neglecting it invites divine punishment unless one repents. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the interplay between ritual observance and spiritual awareness in attaining salvation.
